Prior to version 26.0.37, go/modules/community/bookmarks/controller/Bookmark.php's description() action takes a fully attacker-controlled url parameter and passes it, unvalidated, to \GO\Base\Util\HttpClient::request(). HttpClient::_initRequest() sets CURLOPT_URL directly from this value with no host/IP validation at all. This can result in SSRF via Bookmark/description JMAP action. This issue has been patched in version 26.0.37.
Exposure of PII in Ivanti EPMM before version 12.11.0.0, 12.10.0.1, and 12.9.0.3 allows a remote authenticated attacker with admin privileges to leak GDPR protected user information.

When a message was forwarded inline, edited as new, or had an attachment dragged into a compose window, a specially crafted link attachment (a .desktop file on Linux, or a .url or .lnk file on Windows) was replaced with the content of the file or URL it pointed to when the message was saved or sent. This could disclose local files, or content from the user's network, to the message recipients or to the mail provider.
This bug only affects Thunderbird on Linux and Windows. Other operating systems are unaffected. This vulnerability was fixed in Thunderbird 160 and Thunderbird 153.7.

OpenSearch Dashboards is an open-source data visualization tool designed to work with OpenSearch. From versions 2.14.0 to before 2.19.6, and 3.0.0 to before 3.7.0, a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in OpenSearch Dashboards exists in the fetchDataSourceMetaData route. The sibling test_connection route validates incoming endpoint URLs via isValidURL() against configured endpointDeniedIPs and endpointAllowlistedSuffixes lists, but fetchDataSourceMetaData accepts the same input shape without performing this validation. An authenticated user can supply an internal or loopback endpoint to probe internal network resources. This issue has been patched in versions 2.19.6 and 3.7.0.

Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. Prior to version 0.223.1, Probo's console GraphQL API is a multi-tenant GRC platform where all data is scoped to an organization. A Finding can reference a Risk via finding.riskId. That reference is stored without validating that the risk belongs to the caller's organization, and the Finding.risk field resolver authorizes the finding (caller's org) instead of the risk, then loads the risk with a tenant scope derived from the risk's own global ID. As a result, an authenticated member of organization A can attach an arbitrary organization B risk GID to a finding they own and then read organization B's Risk (name, description, treatment, category, severity, owner) — with no membership in B. The stored cross-tenant reference also blocks B from deleting its own risk (ON DELETE RESTRICT), a cross-tenant integrity/DoS. This issue has been patched in version 0.223.1.

MCUboot's Zephyr serial-recovery upload handler bs_upload() in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c decodes the host-supplied image field of an MCUmgr image-upload request into img_num (a full 32-bit value) and latches it on the off == 0 packet without any range check. It then passes img_num straight to flash_area_id_from_multi_image_slot(img_num, 0), which on the Zephyr port resolves to __flash_area_ids_for_slot() in boot/zephyr/include/sysflash/sysflash.h and indexes the static const int all_slots[] table as all_slots[img_num  2]. That table holds only MCUBOOT_IMAGE_NUMBER  2 entries, so any img_num >= MCUBOOT_IMAGE_NUMBER is an out-of-bounds read.

The path is reachable by anyone with access to the serial / SMP recovery console, which is unauthenticated by design, and the bad value is supplied before any image signature is verified. The defect is specific to the default non-direct upload path (MCUBOOT_SERIAL_DIRECT_IMAGE_UPLOAD disabled) on the Zephyr port with the array-backed slot layout (not CONFIG_SINGLE_APPLICATION_SLOT). It is not gated on a multi-image configuration: MCUBOOT_IMAGE_NUMBER defaults to 1, so even a default single-image build is affected for any image >= 1. The MCUBOOT_SERIAL_DIRECT_IMAGE_UPLOAD path is safe (its flash_area_id_from_direct_image() switch returns -EINVAL for unknown indices).

flash_area_id_from_multi_image_slot() takes a signed int image_index while img_num is uint32_t, so the attacker controls the sign of the index as well as its magnitude: an image of 0xFFFFFFFE converts to -2 and reads all_slots[-4], off the front of the table, while large positive values read off the end (CWE-192). (0xFFFFFFFF itself is the "no image given" sentinel and selects image 0.) Either way the index multiply img * 2 is performed in int, so a wild offset yields a bus/hard fault, giving a reliable denial of service of the bootloader during recovery. For moderately out-of-range indices the read returns adjacent .rodata as a garbage flash-area id that is handed to flash_area_open(); this normally fails with MGMT_ERR_EINVAL, but if the garbage id happens to match a valid non-image partition, the subsequent erase/write can target a partition outside the image set (CWE-787). The attacker-supplied value is never echoed back, so there is no information disclosure. The fix is to reject img_num >= BOOT_IMAGE_NUMBER on the off == 0 packet, before the slot lookup. The comparison must be made on the unsigned img_num: an equivalent guard applied after the conversion to int would not reject the negative case above. __flash_area_ids_for_slot() should bounds-check its own arguments as defence in depth.
This vulnerability was reported independently twice: by NVIDIA Project Vanessa on 2026-06-22, and by Kai Phan (@kaimandalic) on 2026-07-19 as GHSA-8v33-88p6-jffj, which is closed as a duplicate of this advisory. Both original reports are reproduced in full below.

Zipline from 4.2.0 before 4.6.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that logs sensitive environment variable values, such as OAUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET, without redaction at startup. Attackers with access to system journal or docker logs can obtain OAuth2 client secrets and use them to exchange intercepted OAuth2 callbacks for valid tokens.

The WP Ultimate CSV Importer  WordPress plugin before 9.3 does not escape values from imported files before using them in SQL queries when importing LifterLMS content, allowing high privilege users such as admin, including the administrator of a single site on a multisite network, to perform SQL injection attacks.

A vulnerability was found in vllm-project vllm 0.30.0/0.31.0. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file single_type_kv_cache_manager.py of the component Common Prefix Handler. The manipulation results in race condition. The attack may be performed from remote. Attacks of this nature are highly complex. It is stated that the exploitability is difficult. The exploit has been made public and could be used. Upgrading to version 0.32.0 is able to resolve this issue. The patch is identified as e687a251bb056fa527846633f7a1b0a6c0f42374. You should upgrade the affected component.

Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in Blubrry Podcasting PowerPress Podcasting powerpress allows Path Traversal.This issue affects PowerPress Podcasting: from n/a through 11.18.3.

A kernel pool buffer overflow vulnerability in the
ct0531fl.sys file of the Creative WDM Audio Driver (64-bit), Sound Blaster Audigy 4
      and Sound Blaster Audigy 5/Rx could allow a local
attacker with low privilege access to cause a denial of service.

Frappe Framework before 15.123.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the frappe.email.email_body.get_email_html method, which lacks role checks. Authenticated users, including portal Website Users, can inject stylesheet link tags into unescaped email templates, causing Premailer to fetch internal or external hosts and return the content.

BookStack before 26.09.2 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the ZIP content importer that allows authenticated users with the Import Content permission to exhaust server storage. Attackers can upload a small ZIP whose data.json references one bundled file many times, causing ZipImportRunner::importAttachment() to write a full copy per reference.

Vulnerability in Oracle REST Data Services (component: Database Actions).  Supported versions that are affected are 24.2.0-26.1.0. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle REST Data Services.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle REST Data Services accessible data as well as  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle REST Data Services accessible data and unauthorized ability to cause a partial denial of service (partial DOS) of Oracle REST Data Services. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.7 (Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L).

Vulnerability in Oracle REST Data Services (component: Database Actions).  Supported versions that are affected are 24.2.0-26.1.0. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle REST Data Services.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle REST Data Services accessible data as well as  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle REST Data Services accessible data and unauthorized ability to cause a partial denial of service (partial DOS) of Oracle REST Data Services. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.7 (Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L).

In Modem, there is a possible out of bounds write due to a missing bounds check. This could lead to remote denial of service, if a UE has connected to a rogue base station controlled by the attacker, if a malicious actor has already obtained the System privilege. User interaction is needed for exploitation. Patch ID: MOLY01923663 / ALPS11315955; Issue ID: MSV-10866.

OpenAM before 16.1.4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows privileged attackers to inject script by placing markup in a user's display name. When the victim reaches the OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect consent page, the unencoded name executes script that can steal the OpenAM session cookie to impersonate the user.

OpenAM before 16.1.4 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows remote attackers to redirect users after SAML 1.x single sign-on by exploiting loose trusted-partner destination matching. Attackers can craft links to /SAMLAwareServlet or /SAMLPOSTProfileServlet with a destination host resembling a trusted partner to send authenticated users to attacker-controlled phishing sites.

Gwenhywfar 4.99.8beta before 5.14.2 contains a stack-based buffer overflow in GWEN_TLV_Buffer_To_DB() in src/parser/tlv.c when decoding BER-TLV tags into a fixed 128-byte buffer. Attackers can supply a record with about 127 or more tag continuation bytes or a truncated multi-byte tag, such as via a malicious chip card's EF_SSD file read by libchipcard's ZKA driver, to crash the application.

Winter CMS is a content management system built on the Laravel PHP framework. Prior to 1.2.14, BrandSetting::renderCss() and EditorSetting::renderCss() store raw LESS compiler output with Cache::forever() but apply strip_tags() only to the value returned on a cache miss. The first render after saving custom CSS appears sanitized while priming an unsafe cache entry, and later cache hits return unsanitized output into the backend style element, allowing a user with backend.manage_branding or backend.manage_editor to cause stored cross-site scripting when another backend page renders the styles. The styles also appear on unauthenticated backend sign-in, password restore, and password reset layouts. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.14.

In multiple functions of oem_svc_setup.c, there is a possible way to dump secure cache lines into non-secure memory on warm reset due to a missing permission check. This could lead to local information disclosure with System execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

Action View is a framework for handling view template lookup and rendering and provides view helpers for building HTML. Prior to 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2, the fix for CVE-2026-33168 skips blank HTML attribute names in Action View tag helpers, but it tests the name before converting it to a string. A Symbol name made only of whitespace, such as :" ", is not blank, because Symbol#blank? is Symbol#empty?, so it reaches the attribute escaping, which emits an attribute with no name and produces malformed HTML. The asset tag helpers, such as image_tag, video_tag and audio_tag, symbolize their options, so a whitespace String name passed to them takes the same path. A carefully crafted attribute value could then be misinterpreted by the browser as a separate attribute name, possibly leading to XSS. Applications that allow users to specify custom HTML attribute names are affected. This issue is fixed in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2.

Padloc 4.0.0 before 4.3.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the legacy retrieveMFAToken handler that never counts wrong email verification codes toward the attempt limit. Unauthenticated attackers knowing a victim's email can brute force the 6-digit code to obtain verification tokens usable in signup, login and account recovery flows.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Eye Exam (eye_mag) module that allows administrators to inject JavaScript through unencoded Eye_defaults list option titles. Attackers can store a crafted title via edit_list.php that breaks out of a jQuery string in eye_base.php, executing script in any authenticated user's session when they click Defaults.

IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway 1.0.0 through 1.0.11 is vulnerable to cross-site scripting. This vulnerability allows a privileged user to embed arbitrary JavaScript code in the Web UI thus altering the intended functionality potentially leading to credentials disclosure within a trusted session.

A security flaw has been discovered in yangzongzhuan RuoYi up to 4.8.3. Impacted is the function VelocityUtils.getFileName of the file VelocityUtils.java of the component Code Generator. Performing a manipulation of the argument className results in path traversal. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely.

OkHttp through 5.5.1 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in CertificatePinner that skips pin checks because Pin.matchesHostname does not normalize trailing-dot hostnames. Network attackers with a CA-trusted certificate not matching configured pins can intercept or modify TLS traffic when applications request the trailing-dot form of pinned hosts.

Kiwi TCMS before 17.1 contains a hard-coded cryptographic key vulnerability that allows remote attackers to forge signed data by using the publicly known Django SECRET_KEY in tcms/settings/common.py. Attackers can forge or tamper with signed cookie-based messages and django.core.signing payloads, weakening password-reset and session-authentication HMACs on deployments keeping the default.

thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the fetchClientSecret Next.js server action that allows unauthenticated attackers to create Stripe checkout sessions for other teams. Attackers can invoke the action with a forged Team object containing a victim's stripeCustomerId to obtain Growth plan Checkout session client secrets with attacker-influenced return URLs.

NodePress through 8.5.1 contains an HTML injection vulnerability in linesToEmailContent() that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject markup into notification emails because comment content is not escaped. Attackers can post comments or replies via POST /comments containing forged links, images, or tracking resources rendered in administrator and author mail clients from the blog's address.

The ITE IT8xxx2 SHI host-command backend in subsys/mgmt/ec_host_cmd/backends/ec_host_cmd_backend_shi_ite.c arms the SPI peripheral before its receive context exists. shi_ite_init_registers() sets the state machine to SHI_STATE_READY_TO_RECV and calls irq_enable() while the device initializes at POST_KERNEL priority CONFIG_KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEFAULT (40), but data->rx_ctx and data->tx are only assigned later by shi_ite_backend_init(), which ec_host_cmd_init() invokes at CONFIG_EC_HOST_CMD_INIT_PRIORITY (default 80).

If the attached host processor starts a SPI transaction inside that window, the Rx-valid-length interrupt fires, shi_ite_int_handler() passes its state check and calls shi_ite_parse_header(), which stores the host-derived request length through the still-NULL data->rx_ctx. On the IT8xxx2 low addresses are not backed by RAM, and with CONFIG_NULL_POINTER_EXCEPTION_DETECTION_PMP the first bytes of the address space are explicitly made inaccessible, so the store raises a fatal access fault in interrupt context. The window widens further when CONFIG_EC_HOST_CMD_INITIALIZE_AT_BOOT is disabled and the application calls ec_host_cmd_init() itself.

The result is a kernel panic on the embedded controller: with Zephyr's default fatal handler the CPU halts, so the controller stops servicing host commands until a hardware reset. Because the trigger is traffic from the attached host processor -- an untrusted peer from the controller firmware's point of view -- software on that host can provoke the fault by forcing a controller reset and issuing transactions during the reboot, turning a recoverable reset into a persistent outage. Impact is limited to availability: the faulting address is fixed and not attacker-chosen, so no memory-corruption primitive follows.

The fix leaves the interface at SHI_STATE_DISABLED with the interrupt masked during device init, moves irq_enable() into shi_ite_backend_init() after the buffers are published, and makes shi_ite_int_handler() reject a NULL data->rx_ctx while write-clearing IT83XX_SPI_ISR and IT83XX_SPI_RX_VLISR so that an unexpected early interrupt cannot storm.

The Zephyr WebSocket client validates the server's handshake response in on_header_value() in subsys/net/lib/websocket/websocket.c. The comparison was performed as strncmp(at, str, length), where length is the length of the value the server sent rather than the length of the expected value, so the check only asked whether the received value was a prefix of the expected base64(SHA-1(key || GUID)). A server that returned a handful of correct characters passed, and a response carrying an empty Sec-WebSocket-Accept: header caused strncmp() to be called with a count of zero, which returns 0 and set ctx->sec_accept_ok with no comparison performed at all. The header-value callback also cleared ctx->sec_accept_present after the first chunk, so a value split across receive-buffer boundaries was only ever examined in part.

ctx->sec_accept_ok is the sole WebSocket-specific gate in websocket_connect(); the client does not check the HTTP status code or the Upgrade:/Connection: headers. Any HTTP response containing an empty or prefix-matching Sec-WebSocket-Accept header therefore completed the handshake, after which the socket is finalized as a WebSocket and all further peer bytes are parsed as frames. The affected path is driven directly by remote input through subsys/net/lib/http/http_parser.c, and is reached by every user of websocket_connect(), including MQTT over WebSocket (subsys/net/lib/mqtt/mqtt_transport_websocket.c) and subsys/net/lib/ocpp/ocpp.c.

The Sec-WebSocket-Accept exchange is not a secret-based authentication -- an endpoint or on-path attacker that sees the request can compute the expected value -- so the impact is bounded to parties that never observed the handshake request: a caching or transparent intermediary replaying a canned response, an off-path attacker injecting a spoofed response, or a non-WebSocket endpoint the client was induced to talk to. For those, the per-connection binding that RFC 6455 requires the client to enforce provided no protection at all, letting a single crafted response convince the device it holds a live WebSocket session and causing it to send application data to, and accept frames from, an unverified peer. There is no memory-safety consequence.

The fix compares each delivered chunk against the expected value at the position reached so far, refuses a chunk that would overrun it, and accepts only once every byte of the expected value -- and no more -- has been matched; on_header_field() now also clears the flag for any other header so a partial value cannot be continued across an intervening header.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains a stored sql injection vulnerability in the MySQL driver that allows database users with table creation rights to inject SQL through unescaped geometry column names in unconvert_field(). Attackers can craft a column name containing an SQL expression that executes with another AdminNeo user's privileges when they edit a row, save it, or export the table.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authentication bypass in password reset, letting external-identity accounts receive local passwords. Attackers with mailbox access can request reset tokens for OIDC, Keycloak, Entra ID, LDAP, SSO, or WebAuthn accounts and log in locally, skipping IdP MFA and deprovisioning.

Vulnerability in Oracle REST Data Services (component: Core).  Supported versions that are affected are 24.2.0-26.1.0. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle REST Data Services.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle REST Data Services accessible data as well as  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle REST Data Services accessible data. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle REST Data Services.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle REST Data Services accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.3 (Confidentiality impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N).

Tanium addressed an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in Threat Response.

A flaw was found in libstdc++. When a byte-by-byte write operation fails during file stream processing, the library may still append data into the internal memory buffer. An attacker capable of inducing repeated write failures in an affected service can trigger a buffer overflow, potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption.

A out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in the dr_mp3 drmp3_init_internal functionality of dr_libs (version(s): 0.7.3). A specially crafted .mp3 file can lead to an out-of-bounds read. An attacker can provide a malicious file to trigger this vulnerability.

NocoBase is an AI-powered no-code/low-code platform for building business applications and enterprise solutions. Versions 2.1.0 through 2.1.14 contain a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the customRequests:send endpoint. A low-privileged authenticated user can override the stored request URL at runtime using options.url, causing the NocoBase server to send requests to attacker-controlled or internal destinations. Exploitation could expose internal services, Docker host gateways, or cloud metadata endpoints and allow the server to be used as a trusted network proxy. This issue has been fixed in version 2.1.15.

Winter CMS is a content management system built on the Laravel PHP framework. From 1.2.13 until 1.2.14, the Backend\Controllers\MyAccount controller inherits the FormController actions create, update, and preview while declaring an empty $requiredPermissions array, and formFindModelObject() resolves a caller-supplied record identifier through an unscoped Backend\Models\User query. Any authenticated backend user can request another sequential user identifier through /backend/backend/myaccount/preview/{other_user_id} or the inherited update action and read profile data including name, login, email, avatar, role, group membership, superuser status, and throttle state. Password material is not exposed, and existing model authorization guards block cross-user writes. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.14.
Out-Of-Bounds Read in the MSI-X table in the QVM could allow an attacker in the guest to cause an information disclosure or a crash of the QVM.

Viber for iOS through 29.4.0.24 fails to validate the logical screen width and height in received GIF headers, allowing attackers to crash the app. Attackers can send a crafted GIF with zero dimensions that triggers an uncaught NSInternalInconsistencyException, aborting the app with SIGABRT when opened.

Semantic MediaWiki 3.0.0 before 7.4.1 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in the ElasticStore ConceptDescriptionInterpreter that only detects directly self-referencing concepts. Users with page-edit rights can create mutually referencing concept pages, causing concept page views, Special:Ask, or api.php action=ask queries to exhaust PHP memory or stack.

Sleipnir Mobile for iPhone / iPad and Sleipnir Mobile for iPhone / iPad Black Edition provided by Fenrir Inc. are vulnerable to improper certificate verification. A man-in-the-middle attack may allow an attacker to eavesdrop on an encrypted communication.

Contao 4.0.0 before 5.3.54, 5.4.0 before 5.7.17, and 6.0.0 before 6.0.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows content editors to read image files anywhere on the filesystem via the {{image::}} insert tag. Attackers can embed percent-encoded sequences like ..%2f that pass Validator::isInsecurePath() before rawurldecode(), making the frontend resize and serve readable image files outside the files directory.

A per-host mutual-TLS authorization bypass in Node.js lets a client authorized for the default hostname reach a protected hostname it is not authorized for. When a TLS server assigns a hostname a different client-certificate CA with `server.addContext(host, { ca: protectedCA })` but no server certificate in that SNI context, the per-host client CA is never installed and the handshake falls back to the default client CA. In `src/crypto/crypto_tls.cc`, `CertCbDone` installs the SNI context's CA only when `setSniContext` succeeds, but `setSniContext` returns `false` for a context with no server certificate, so a CA-only SNI context silently keeps the default CA. A client holding a certificate trusted by the default CA, but not the protected CA, can therefore complete mTLS to the protected hostname and read its response even with `requestCert` and `rejectUnauthorized` enabled, while a client certified by the protected CA is rejected. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

Missing rate limiting, per-account submission quota and geographic validation in the publicar_aviso RPC function in Lagarto Chivato 0.4.1 and earlier on Web allows remote authenticated attackers to flood the moderation queue via unlimited submission of notices with arbitrary coordinates.

A security vulnerability has been detected in Moonshot AI Kimi Code up to 2.5.2. This affects the function isOriginAllowed of the file apps/kimi-code/dist-web/assets/index-HU0LCM-X.js of the component Web UI. Such manipulation of the argument kimi_origin leads to open redirect. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
Information leak in Skia in Google Chrome prior to 157.0.8103.78 allowed a remote attacker to obtain cross-origin data via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: High)

Missing release of memory after effective lifetime vulnerability in openEuler iSulad on Linux.

This vulnerability is associated with program file src/daemon/modules/spec/specs_mount.c.



This issue affects iSulad: through 2.1.6.



The memory leak vulnerability causes the iSulad daemon to be triggered frequently, exhausting the host machine's memory and ultimately leading to an OOM crash of the daemon, resulting in a denial of service (DoS).
A missing authorization vulnerability in the Promotion API in Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) before 7.3.2-86009-5 and 7.4.1-90080-1 allows remote authenticated users to write specific files.

An improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory vulnerability in the contentextract in Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) before 7.3.2-86009-5 and 7.4.1-90080-1 allows remote authenticated users to read specific files.

A server-side request forgery vulnerability in the Credential API in Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) before 7.3.2-86009-5 and 7.4.1-90080-1 allows remote authenticated users to read specific files.
A missing authorization vulnerability in the SocketIo API in Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) before 7.3.2-86009-5 and 7.4.1-90080-1 allows remote authenticated users to write specific files.
A missing authorization vulnerability in the TaskScheduler API in Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) before 7.3.2-86009-5 and 7.4.1-90080-1 allows remote authenticated users to write specific files.

An external control of system or configuration setting vulnerability in the synomount in Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) before 7.3.2-86009-5 and 7.4.1-90080-1 allows remote authenticated users to write specific files.

BookStack before 26.09.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in ImageController::checkImagePermission() that allows authenticated non-admin users to bypass page-level content restrictions for images whose owning page has been moved to the recycle bin, because the permission check relies on Page::getPage() which returns null for soft-deleted pages and silently skips the PageView check. Attackers can enumerate sequential image IDs via GET /images/edit/{id} to disclose metadata of restricted images, and users with image-update-all/image-delete-all privileges can rename, replace, or permanently delete images belonging to content they cannot view, persisting the damage even after the page is restored.

ToolJet before 3.21.94, fixed in commit e5f387a, contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the app environments init endpoint that allows authenticated users to read app version metadata belonging to other workspaces. Attackers can send GET requests to /api/app-environments/init with an editing_version_id from another workspace to retrieve the version name, description, status, current environment ID, and app ID, because the lookup is not scoped to the caller's organization.

Zipline before 4.2.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the /api/user/files/transaction endpoint that allows authenticated users to modify other users' files due to absent ownership checks. Attackers who know a target file ID can submit transaction requests to edit or delete files belonging to any user.

NocoDB before 2026.06.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the profile update handler in users.service.ts, which returns the stored user record without passing it through the user-serialization filter, exposing the bcrypt password hash, salt, and session token counter. Attackers holding a stolen or hijacked session can update the profile to retrieve that account's password hash and salt for offline cracking.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in ObservationController::deleteAction that allows attackers to delete observation form records without a CSRF token. Attackers can lure a logged-in clinician to a page issuing a GET to delete.php with guessed id values, soft-deleting observations in the victim's open encounter.

Missing authentication for a critical function (CWE-306) in the management service (uavmonitor_usbv1) of the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an unauthenticated attacker on the local network to read device information, such as the serial number, MAC address, IP address and radio configuration, and to change configuration settings. The service accepts commands in DJI's proprietary DUML protocol without any authentication. Exploitation requires network access to TCP port 16000 on the board and that the unit is not connected to another controlling host. The same commands are also accepted over the USB operator port. Confirmed on a physical device.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.
Dell PowerStore contains a content-injection vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability to display misleading text on the genuine login page for phishing.

The Countdown, Coming Soon, Maintenance  WordPress plugin through 3.0.8 does not check that the user is allowed to browse content before returning post titles from one of its AJAX actions, allowing any authenticated user, such as a subscriber, to list the titles of published entries of any post type, including types that WordPress does not expose to them. Draft, private and pending content is not returned; only published entries are disclosed.

The Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 does not check that a user duplicating a post is allowed to edit it, which, when the slug takeover option is enabled, allows users of a role an administrator has given Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 access to, such as Contributor, to move any readable post off its permalink and publish their copy at that address.

The Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 does not check whether a user may publish posts when duplicating one, allowing users of a role an administrator has given Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 access to, such as Contributors, to create published posts, including posts attributed to other users.

A weakness has been identified in Akaunting up to 3.3.0. The affected element is the function calculation_to_quantity of the file helpers.php of the component Invoice Item Validation. Executing a manipulation of the argument quantity can lead to numeric range comparison without minimum check. The attack may be performed from remote. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A flaw has been found in Opixido OCMS up to b7c15660aba83d96677c1a9abaa69c082a24f21c. This impacts an unknown function of the file admin/TUI/index.php of the component Admin TUI. This manipulation of the argument img causes cross site scripting. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Continious delivery with rolling releases is used by this product. Therefore, no version details of affected nor updated releases are available. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Zr.Admin.NET commit 1845017 through commit eb9228a contains a missing authorization vulnerability in TasksController.Get that allows any logged-in user to read scheduled task details without the monitor:job permission. Attackers can obtain task ids from the unprotected /monitor/jobLog/list endpoint and retrieve job parameters, API URLs, cron expressions, and stored SQL statements.

The Burst Statistics  WordPress plugin before 3.7.5 does not enforce a shared report's date range on the analytics it serves to the report's share link, allowing anyone holding the link to read the report's statistics for any period the site retains rather than the period the report was shared for.

GeoPulse 1.5.0 through 2.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in GET /api/v1/places/geocoding/{id} that allows authenticated users to read other users' private locations. Attackers can enumerate sequential reverse_geocoding_location ids to retrieve other users' custom place names, city, country, coordinates and bounding boxes from their history.

Netcccyun dnsmgr 2.18 before 2.22 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in POST /cloudflare/get_domain_default_line that allows restricted users to access domains outside their permissions. Restricted sub-users or single-domain logins can iterate the domain_id parameter to enumerate panel domain ids and read each domain's DNS line list and default line.

When a file is edited in a fork through the web editor, Gitea can first copy a branch from the base repository into the fork. That copy did not check whether the user may read the base repository's code. A user who had forked a repository and later lost access to it, for example after it was made private or they were removed as a collaborator, could keep copying its current branches into their fork and read them. The copy now requires read access to the code of the base repository.

The AGit flow (pushing to `refs/for/...`) did not check the pusher's access to pull requests again when it created the pull request. A user or deploy key with read access to the code only, or with write access to the wiki over SSH, could open pull requests in a repository where they have no access to pull requests. Creating a pull request through AGit now requires read access to the pull requests of the repository and is refused for wiki pushes.

`GET /api/v1/users/{username}/orgs/{org}/permissions` only checked that the organization is visible to the caller and then returned the named user's role in it. Any signed-in user could learn whether another user is an owner, admin or member of a public or limited organization, including for members who conceal their membership. The roles are now only returned to the user themselves, to members of the organization and to site administrators.

Dinky through 1.2.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in ClusterConfigurationController that allows authenticated users without cluster configuration permissions to list Flink cluster configurations. Attackers can query the /api/clusterConfiguration/list and listAll endpoints to retrieve full configJson deployment settings for every cluster in their tenant.

thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows remote attackers to send users to arbitrary sites by supplying an unvalidated redirectUri parameter on the /pay/[id] payment link page. Attackers can distribute payment links with a malicious redirectUri that PayPageWidget opens via window.open after payment without noopener, enabling phishing and reverse tabnabbing of the payment page.

thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read non-public team metadata by requesting the team join page with any invite ID. Attackers who know a team slug can obtain the serialized Team object, exposing billing email, billing status, Stripe customer ID, verified domain and support identifiers.

Keystatic through 0.6.9 contains a login cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the githubOauthCallback handler that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to sign victims in with the attacker's GitHub account by omitting state validation. Attackers can induce victims to visit the OAuth callback with an attacker-obtained authorization code, causing victim edits in the admin UI to be committed under the attacker's GitHub identity.

An out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in VideoLAN VLC 3.0.23. By using a specially crafted NUV file, an attacker could exploit this vulnerability to perform an out-of-bounds read, potentially leading to the disclosure of sensitive information.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. Prior to 6.2.13, a CMS user who can edit records through a GridField detail form can send a direct save request that creates a new record even when the user does not have permission to create that record type. The server-side save path checks edit access but does not enforce the required create permission before persistence. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. Prior to 6.2.13, a CMS user who can edit a record through a GridField detail form can submit a user-controlled ClassName value to change the record into an unrelated class without the create and edit permission checks required for that target class. This permits an unauthorized record type change outside the GridField's intended model hierarchy. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. Prior to 6.2.13, PermissionCheckboxSetField accepts permission codes that the field did not offer and stores them without an allowlist, then renders permission codes without escaping them. A user with access to the Security section can save attacker-controlled content as a permission code, causing JavaScript to execute in the browser of another user who views the field. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

libspdm is a sample implementation that follows the DMTF SPDM specifications. Prior to 3.8.3 and 4.0.0-rc2, libspdm_x509_verify_cert_chain() in os_stub/cryptlib_openssl/pk/x509.c and os_stub/cryptlib_mbedtls/pk/x509.c validates certificate signatures one link at a time instead of validating the complete X.509 path. In deployments using a pinned root with a constrained multi-tier PKI, an attacker holding a valid issuer credential below a constrained CA can present a subordinate certificate that exceeds pathLenConstraint or nameConstraints and may be accepted for SPDM identity validation. Exploitation requires the application to use libspdm's backend validation without an additional certificate-chain validation mechanism, the pinned root cannot be substituted, and the deployment's measurement policy must allow identity impersonation alone to satisfy its acceptance requirements. The mbedTLS backend remains unable to enforce nameConstraints because upstream mbedTLS does not implement that check. The full-chain validation changes are released in versions 3.8.3 and 4.0.0-rc2.
Missing Authorization vulnerability in ThimPress LearnPress learnpress allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects LearnPress: from n/a through 4.4.13.

Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS) vulnerability in Automattic WP Job Manager wp-job-manager allows Code Injection.This issue affects WP Job Manager: from n/a through 2.4.10.
Missing Authorization vulnerability in weDevs WP ERP erp allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects WP ERP: from n/a through 1.17.11.

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260701.0, the caseIncidentAdd, caseRfiAdd, and caseRftAdd GraphQL mutations require only authentication and do not require a capability check. An authenticated user with reader-level permissions can therefore create incident, request-for-information, and request-for-takedown case objects regardless of the user's assigned role, causing unauthorized changes to platform data. This issue is fixed in version 7.260701.0.

SplitPro through 2.1.6 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the addOrEditExpense and addOrEditCurrencyConversion tRPC mutations that allows authenticated users to assign expenses to arbitrary users. Attackers can enumerate sequential user IDs and supply them in participants or paidBy fields to fabricate debts on victims' balances, even in unseen groups.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privilege users to read unpublished FAQ titles via bookmark_action. Attackers can request FAQ detail pages with bookmark_action=add across sequential ids, then view /user/bookmarks to reveal draft and pending submission question text.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an improper reference counting flaw on multisite deployments, allowing editors to delete other instances' attachment files. Because linkedRecords() counts only the local faqattachment table, deleting an attachment with shared md5 content makes File::delete() unlink the shared blob, destroying another instance's files.

phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha.2 before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows category- or language-restricted editors to bypass scoped rights via public REST write endpoints. Attackers with a scoped right and the shared API token can use PUT faq/update, POST faq/create, and POST category to rewrite published FAQs and create root categories outside their scope.

phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha.2 before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in POST /admin/api/faq/import that lets FAQ_ADD users bypass the FAQ_PUBLISH right. Authenticated contributors can upload a CSV with column 8 set to true to publish unreviewed, optionally sticky FAQs such as phishing content.

phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows FAQ_EDIT users to bypass SvgSanitizer using namespace-prefixed elements like <x:script>. Attackers can upload malicious SVGs through the admin image upload so script runs in the site origin on IIS, hijacking sessions of users like super-admins.

phpMyFAQ through 4.1.12 and from 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the admin FAQ copy and translate pages, which check only global FAQ_ADD or FAQ_TRANSLATE rights. Authenticated add-only or category-scoped editors can open any FAQ to read drafts, ACL-restricted records, private notes, and author e-mail addresses.

phpMyFAQ 4.1.9 before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an improper restriction of excessive authentication attempts vulnerability in PasswordChangeController::update() that bypasses the step-up throttle. Attackers holding a hijacked admin-area session can repeatedly guess faqpassword_old with a reusable CSRF token to learn the original password and take over the account.

phpMyFAQ 4.1.9 before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows attackers holding a hijacked session to enroll passkeys using only the session and webauthn CSRF token. Attackers can call /api/webauthn/prepare and /api/webauthn/register to replace the owner's passkeys, gaining persistent passwordless login that survives password changes and resets.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in FileUploadPlugin that allows database users to store script-bearing SVG files by uploading unsanitized content. Attackers can upload a malicious SVG to a *_path field, executing script in the same-origin session of any administrator who opens the file link.

phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha.2 before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows language-scoped editors to read other translations by checking FAQ_EDIT against the route language but loading the ?lang= UI-language row. Attackers can request the admin.faq.edit route with an authorized language and a different lang parameter to read drafts, private notes, author e-mails and revisions.

IBM API Connect 12.1.0.0 through 12.1.1.2 could allow an authenticated privileged attacker to send unauthorized requests from the system due to server-side request forgery. This could be used to enumerate network resources or to support further attacks.
Improper Input Validation in a procnto message handler could allow an attacker with local access to send a crafted message which can cause an information disclosure in the QNX Neutrino kernel

Invalid Pointer Reference in the TimerSettime() system call could allow an attacker with local access to arm a crafted timer event which can cause an information disclosure in the QNX Neutrino kernel.

A improper privilege management vulnerability in Fortinet FortiManager 8.0.0, FortiManager 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiManager 7.2.0 through 7.2.12, FortiManager Cloud 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiManager Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager Cloud 7.4.1 through 7.4.11, FortiManager Cloud 7.2.1 through 7.2.12 may allow an authenticated administrator to escalate their privileges, bypass authorization controls or impersonate internal services via specially crafted requests to the GUI.
IBM Cyber Fraud 1.0.0 through 1.1.0 could allow an attacker with local access to a container to extract sensitive information due to unrestrictive network policies.

IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway 1.0.0 through 1.0.11 is vulnerable to improper access control in the bulk import path. A remote authenticated attacker holding a team-scoped `admin.import` permission can overwrite the endpoint URL, request headers, and authentication credentials of public tools, resources, and prompts owned by other tenants by sending a crafted POST request to `/v1/import` with `conflict_strategy=update`, redirecting subsequent AI gateway invocations to an attacker-controlled host.

The RegistrationMagic  WordPress plugin before 6.1.0.4 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before using it in a SQL statement, which could allow high privilege users such as admin to perform SQL injection attacks.
HCL MyXalytics was affected by Improper Input validation Vulnerability. It allow malicious or unexpected data to cause unintended system behaviour or security issues.

HCL MyXalytics was affected by Content Spoofing Vulnerability. It may allow an attacker to manipulate displayed content, making it appear as though it originates from a trusted source, potentially leading to phishing or data theft.
HCL MyXalytics was affected by Potential DOS Vulnerability. It allows users to input data without any restriction on the number of characters which can impact system performance or availability.

Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle REST Data Services accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 3.7 (Confidentiality impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N).

Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a partial denial of service (partial DOS) of Siebel Apps - Marketing. A security vulnerability has been detected in iomad up to 4.5.15/5.0.11/5.1.8/5.2.4. Affected by this issue is the function store_temporary_password of the file public/local/iomad/classes/company_user.php of the component Password Field Handler. Such manipulation leads to information disclosure. The attack may be performed from remote. The attack requires a high level of complexity. The exploitation is known to be difficult. The name of the patch is 0d9c0ccaa8a77583f5dd92eb7be7fbbb8cc6ec9b/9c740fd254fd12d56d7be3b85ac5e9fb4f8c03d8/33755cdd551a84be423b1eaf784d405c1988dbad/7fcf9b52c539a67f3e46a8da6b42ab1d1f26295b. It is advisable to implement a patch to correct this issue. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

A security flaw has been discovered in sunkaifei FlyCMS up to e71738e0cfb7ffd48c2ce74242a2dbb43f84f25a. Affected by this vulnerability is the function ModelDataService.insertData of the file articles/detail.html of the component Content Rendering. Performing a manipulation of the argument content results in cross site scripting. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. Continious delivery with rolling releases is used by this product. Therefore, no version details of affected nor updated releases are available. The patch is named 714521a9262e7bc9ca5713c873f57e96a4845352. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.3, ed25519.verify() decodes a public key in crypto_sign_open() without rejecting small-order points or their non-canonical encodings. With S = 0 and a small-order R value, an attacker who can choose the public key can produce signatures that verify for many messages, or all messages with the identity key, without a private key. This can defeat proof-of-possession, attribution, non-repudiation, or deduplication checks that rely on a signature being bound to the message. Keys produced by normal Ed25519 key generation are not small-order, so applications that verify only trusted or internally generated public keys are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.3.

CAI Content Credentials is affected by an Improper Input Validation vulnerability that could result in a Security feature bypass. An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to bypass security measures and gain unauthorized limited write access. Exploit depends on conditions beyond the attacker's control. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction.

Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. Prior to version 0.224.0, the public Trust Center GraphQL API exposes Query.node(id:) with @authentication(required: OPTIONAL) — an unauthenticated internet visitor to any published trust center can call it. Six of its type branches — Organization, Framework, Audit, ThirdParty (subprocessor), TrustCenter, and TrustCenterReference — resolve the object with a tenant scope derived from the client-supplied GID itself (coredata.NewScopeFromObjectID(id)) and load it with a bare Get(scope, id) that performs no comparison to the current trust center's OrganizationID and no showOnTrustCenter/visibility check. (The Document and File branches, by contrast, correctly pass trustCenter.OrganizationID and check visibility). This issue has been patched in version 0.224.0.

Philips Hue Bridge Pro Argument Injection Restricted File Write Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to modify files on affected installations of Philips Hue Bridge Pro. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code within a container on the target system, in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the factory data service, which listens on TCP port 5001 by default. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to execute a system call. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to modify files in the context of the service account. Was ZDI-CAN-33090.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a predictable token generation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge the shared-calendar iCal share token by deriving md5Id() from predictable fields such as object creation time, which is self-disclosed through autorDate and the iCal CREATED field. Attackers can compute the creation minute and forge the md5Id token to access and read a shared calendar's iCal feed without authorization.

The WP Ultimate CSV Importer  WordPress plugin before 9.2, WP Ultimate CSV Importer Pro WordPress plugin before 9.0.7 do not protect the files created by their single post export feature, writing them to a publicly accessible location under a predictable name, allowing unauthenticated attackers to download the content and custom fields of any exported post, including non-public content.

A weakness has been identified in Mereithhh VanBlog up to 0.54.0. This affects an unknown part of the file packages/server/src/types/access/access.ts of the component Image Upload Endpoint. Executing a manipulation can lead to cross site scripting. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was found in sergix44 XBackBone up to 3.8.2. Impacted is the function MediaController::getRawById of the file app/Controllers/MediaController.php. The manipulation results in cross site scripting. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

The Burst Statistics  WordPress plugin before 3.7.5 does not check that a reported page view belongs to published content, nor check post status before listing post titles and links in its public statistics output, allowing unauthenticated attackers to disclose the titles and permalinks of draft, pending and private posts.

With `REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW = true`, the Git LFS endpoints still answered unauthenticated requests for repositories that are not private. An anonymous client who knows the path of such a repository and the SHA-256 of an LFS object could download the object, and could use the batch endpoint to test whether an object exists. The Git LFS endpoints now require authentication when sign-in is required to view the instance.

The Kadence Memberships WordPress plugin before 4.0.6 does not check that the membership level submitted when renewing a membership matches the level being renewed, pricing the renewal from the submitted level while activating the membership at its own level, allowing unauthenticated users to activate a paid membership without paying on sites that also offer a free level.

@fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart form data used by Fastify. In versions 3.2.1 through 3.2.5, the parser can interpret the same multipart bytes differently depending on how they are split across socket reads: when the sequence that terminates a part's header block arrives split exactly at the configured header size limit, an off by one error drops the final header line, so a part declared as a binary file attachment is emitted as an ordinary text field instead of a file. A remote client controls both the multipart body and the header padding needed to reach the boundary and can influence segmentation, so an application that applies upload validation such as malware scanning or extension checks only to file events while trusting plain field values may process the payload through the wrong path. The parser level type confusion is fully reproducible, while the downstream validation bypass depends on the application. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, which tracks how many terminator bytes were actually buffered when the limit is reached so a split terminator no longer corrupts the final header, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. As a workaround, apply the same validation to field values as to file uploads rather than treating file events as a trust boundary.

Weblate 2026.6 through 2026.11.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in ChangeManager.last_changes() that exposes workspaces the viewer cannot view by skipping Workspace.can_view() checks site-wide. Anonymous visitors on instances with REQUIRE_LOGIN disabled and only public projects can query /changes/, /api/changes/, or RSS/CSV feeds to obtain hidden workspace names, UUIDs, actions, and timestamps.

Unrolled Secure before 1.18.0 contains an SSLRedirect bypass vulnerability in Secure.isSSL() that trusts the client-supplied r.URL.Scheme to determine HTTPS transport. Attackers can send plaintext HTTP requests with an absolute-form https:// request-target to skip the HTTPS redirect and have application responses served unencrypted.

Guard Core is an API security core engine for the FastAPI-Guard, FlaskAPI Guard, and DjAPI Guard adapters. From 1.0.0 until 3.13.0, ContentPreprocessor.preprocess() in guard_core/detection_engine/preprocessor.py collapses all whitespace before built-in pattern matching in the default enhanced mode. This removes carriage returns and newlines required by the http_split and newline-anchored cmd_injection detectors in guard_core/handlers/suspatterns_handler.py, making those detectors unable to match. Framework-decoded CRLF can therefore pass through Guard Core unflagged while the downstream application still receives the raw newline-bearing value. Direct security impact requires a downstream stack or application that persists or re-emits the value into a CRLF-tolerant response or command context. This issue is fixed in version 3.13.0.

The Libreswan IKEv2 state machine did not verify that an IKE_INTERMEDIATE exchange was required to satisfy the addke= PostQuantum algorithm component of the exchange. A connecting client could (maliciously or by implementation error) skip the IKE_INTERMEDIATE exchange and start an IKE_AUTH exchange prematurely. The result is as if the addke= option had not been specified, and such connections are only protected by the classic key exchange algorithm (such as P-256 or Curve25519), allowing "store now, decrypt later" attacks once a quantum computer becomes available. Only connections with the addke= keyword in the ike= and/or esp= configuration option are affected. PostQuantum Hybrid Key Exchange support was added in version 5.4.

The websocket client's HTTP header callback on_header_value() in subsys/net/lib/websocket/websocket.c receives the Sec-WebSocket-Accept header value as a pointer/length pair from the HTTP parser. The referenced bytes live inside the application-supplied receive buffer and are not NUL terminated. When the received value did not match the expected accept key, the pointer was passed directly to a %s conversion in a NET_DBG() call, so the logging code measured the string with strlen() and read on past the end of the header value looking for a terminator.

The value is supplied by the peer during the WebSocket handshake, before any application-level authentication, so a malicious or man-in-the-middle server reached over a ws:// (or otherwise attacker-terminated) connection can trigger the mismatch branch at will simply by answering with a wrong accept key. By sizing the response so the header value ends at the tail of the buffer passed to websocket_connect() as wreq->tmp_buf, the peer can make the scan run off the end of that buffer and into adjacent memory. The defective log statement is compiled in only when websocket debug logging is enabled (CONFIG_NET_WEBSOCKET_LOG_LEVEL_DBG=y, or CONFIG_LOG_DEFAULT_LEVEL=4); it is absent from a default build, which bounds exposure to diagnostic configurations.

The consequence is an out-of-bounds read whose contents are emitted to the log stream: memory adjacent to the receive buffer is disclosed wherever the device's logs are collected or displayed. On targets where the memory following the buffer is not mapped, the scan can instead fault and terminate the connection or thread. No out-of-bounds write occurs, so there is no integrity impact.

The fix copies at most sizeof(got) - 1 bytes of the parser-provided slice into a bounded stack buffer, NUL terminates the copy, and logs that instead, so the formatter never reads beyond the bytes the parser actually offered.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows delegated group or user admins to remove rights they do not hold by submitting empty rights lists. Attackers can send an empty rightIds or userRights array to group/permissions or user/update-rights to wipe all rights of more-privileged groups or administrators.

phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha.2 before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in DELETE /admin/api/faq/delete that lets language-scoped FAQ_DELETE admins bypass their language scope. Attackers can submit a faqId with an in-scope faqLanguage lacking a translation to wipe shared ACL, tags, votes, comments, and attachments of other translations.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains a filter injection vulnerability in its MongoDB driver that allows attackers to affect other documents by embedding ' AND ' or ') OR (' delimiters in a string _id or searched value. Attackers who can store a crafted document can cause a victim's delete or edit to match unintended documents, deleting the entire collection or modifying another document.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha.2 before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated editors to manipulate search index documents by supplying an arbitrary solutionId to the /admin/api/faq/update endpoint. On Elasticsearch or OpenSearch deployments, category-restricted editors can remove published FAQs from search, overwrite other FAQs' search documents, or plant entries that remain searchable after unpublishing.
Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition in the virtio network virtual device could allow an attacker in the guest to manipulate the virtual network device causing a crash of the QVM.
Stack-based Buffer Overflow in the ACPI event handler of the QVM could allow an attacker in a guest to crash the QVM by sending a crafted ACPI request.

IBM Bob 2.0.3 allows unauthorized extensions to retrieve session tokens via the authentication provider API. The token is exposed in the account identifier field during account enumeration, without requiring explicit user consent. This may allow malicious extensions to access sensitive session information and potentially perform unauthorized actions on behalf of the user.

iSponsorBlockTV is a SponsorBlock client for YouTube TV clients. Prior to 2.11.0, src/iSponsorBlockTV/dial_client.py trusts the SSDP LOCATION URL supplied by a local-network responder without validating its destination. During automatic discovery, this can cause an attacker-directed GET request and a constrained POST request to a path ending in /YouTube; the POST uses application-defined headers and an application-defined payload rather than attacker-selected request contents. The requests can reach internal services, but the detailed request behavior states that response data and errors are not returned to the attacker, making the demonstrated behavior blind SSRF with bounded integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 2.11.0.

Docmost is open-source collaborative wiki and documentation software. Prior to 0.96.0, two concurrent role-demotion requests from a space admin or workspace owner can each pass the last-admin or last-owner count check before either update is committed because the validation and role update are not serialized in one transaction. The requests can therefore demote the final two space admins or workspace owners and leave the affected space without an admin or the workspace without an owner, preventing normal administrative recovery. This issue is fixed in version 0.96.0.

The Synopsys DesignWare I3C controller driver (drivers/i3c/i3c_dw.c) tracks free Device Address Table (DAT) slots with get_free_pos(), which signals an exhausted table by returning -1. The helper declared its return type as uint8_t, so the sentinel was truncated to 255, and both consumers (dw_i3c_attach_device() and dw_i3c_i2c_attach_device()) also stored it in a uint8_t before testing if (pos < 0) — a comparison that is never true for an unsigned value. The exhaustion guard was therefore inert in every build.

With the guard defeated, an attach attempted on a full DAT proceeds with pos == 255: it writes data->dw_i3c_i2c_priv_data[255].id, more than 200 bytes past the end of the 32-element dw_i3c_i2c_priv_data array and past the end of struct dw_i3c_data; it stores the resulting out-of-bounds address in desc->controller_priv, from which later detach, reattach and IBI operations read the slot index back; and it performs a 32-bit MMIO store 1020 bytes beyond the hardware DAT base, outside the table the controller reports. The attach still returns success, so the upper layer believes the device is bound.

The DAT is smaller than the software array (its depth is read from DEVICE_ADDR_TABLE_POINTER, commonly 8 or 16 entries), so exhaustion is reachable. In a dual-role build (CONFIG_I3C_DUAL_ROLE with CONFIG_I3C_USE_IBI) acting as a secondary controller, the attach count is supplied by the bus's active controller: i3c_sec_handoffed() attaches one device per entry of the received DEFTGTS list, so a hostile or malfunctioning controller on the local I3C bus that declares more targets than the local DAT depth triggers the condition once per surplus entry. Exhaustion can also be reached from a devicetree that declares more devices than the table holds, or by repeated i3c attach shell commands.

Impact is bounded: the out-of-bounds store is a single byte of fixed value at a fixed displacement, with no attacker-chosen data or offset, so the realistic outcomes are corruption of neighbouring static driver state, writes into reserved controller registers, and inconsistent driver bookkeeping (a crash or a wedged I3C bus) rather than a controllable memory-write primitive. The attack vector is the local chip-to-chip I3C bus; there is no network-reachable path.

phpMyFAQ 3.2.5 before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the user/request-removal API endpoint that lets authenticated users file account removal requests as other users. The ownership check calls getUserById() with the attacker-supplied userId on the session user object, so it compares the input against the target's own record. Attackers who know a victim's login name and email can submit that userId, loginname, and email, sending administrators a spoofed Remove User Request email. This may lead an admin to delete the victim's account and data.

phpMyFAQ 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated frontend users to receive restricted FAQ titles by subscribing to Web Push notifications. When editors publish user/group-restricted FAQs, WebPushService::sendToAll() delivers the question, FAQ id, category, and slugified URL to every subscriber, bypassing the FAQ ACL.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains a reflected HTML injection vulnerability that allows remote attackers to inject markup by supplying crafted array keys in the where URL parameter. Attackers can trick logged-in users into opening a link whose unescaped keys land in select search form name attributes, enabling meta refresh redirects and content spoofing.

Vulnerability in Oracle REST Data Services (component: Core).  Supported versions that are affected are 24.2.0-26.1.0. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle REST Data Services.  Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle REST Data Services accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 3.1 (Confidentiality impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N).

Vulnerability in Oracle REST Data Services (component: Core).  Supported versions that are affected are 24.2.0-26.1.0. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle REST Data Services.  Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle REST Data Services accessible data as well as  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle REST Data Services accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 3.1 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N).

Vulnerability in the Siebel Apps - Marketing product of Oracle Siebel CRM (component: Marketing).  Supported versions that are affected are 17.0-26.9. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a partial denial of service (partial DOS) of Siebel Apps - Marketing. Vulnerability in the Helidon product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: helidon-cors).  Supported versions that are affected are 4.0.0-4.5.5.
